chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the food of those who were Given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The grains and the vegetables.'

key_terms.أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ: Given the Book (People of the Book)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'food of the People of the Book' being lawful for Muslims?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) offers a restrictive interpretation of Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:5, limiting the permissibility of the 'food of the People of the Book' to plant-based items like grains and vegetables. This view contrasts with other scholarly opinions that include meat, highlighting the Shia juristic principle of caution (ihtiyat) in dietary laws by excluding animal products unless specifically slaughtered according to Islamic rites. The hadith underscores the distinction between general permissibility and the specific conditions applied by the Imams to ensure ritual purity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, form Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:5] and the food of those who have been Given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. So heasws said: ‘The grains and the vegetables’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from abu al-Jarud who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘The food of the people to whom the book was given is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them.’ [5:5] He (the Imam) said, ‘It is grains and vegetables.’”
